stories.title: Cisco Warns of New Zero-Day ISE Auth Bypass (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Active Attacks
stories.abstract: Cisco has patched a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in its Identity Services Engine. The flaw, which carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, stems from inadequate API endpoint security and is currently being exploited by malicious actors in real-world attacks.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to sensitive network management infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Cisco Identity Services Engine to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: ABB Ability Edgenius
CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of a SQL injection vulnerability, CVE-2026-76461, affecting its Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager products. CISA has added this flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, mandating urgent remediation for federal agencies.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows attackers to gain unauthorized access or control over email infrastructure, making it a high-priority target for active exploitation.
stories.action: Update Cisco Secure Email Gateway and Web Manager to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
stories.abstract: Google has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-58704, a high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability within the Pixel cellular modem. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing risks of unauthorized access and potential device compromise.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows attackers to bypass permissions, granting them elevated control over affected Pixel devices.
stories.action: Apply the September 2026 Android security updates immediately.

stories.title: Acronis cPanel Backup Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in Targeted Attacks
stories.abstract: A high-severity local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM is currently being exploited in targeted attacks. The flaw stems from insecure file permissions, allowing unauthorized users to gain elevated system access.
stories.why: Exploitation of this vulnerability allows attackers to escalate privileges on compromised web hosting servers, potentially leading to full system takeover.
stories.action: Update the Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: China-Aligned FamousSparrow Deploys SparroWocky Backdoor Across Latin America
stories.abstract: The state-sponsored threat group FamousSparrow is actively compromising government entities throughout Latin America. The attackers are utilizing a newly identified, modular C++ backdoor dubbed SparroWocky to facilitate espionage operations within the region.
stories.why: This indicates an expansion of Chinese-aligned cyber-espionage efforts targeting government infrastructure, necessitating heightened monitoring of regional network traffic and endpoint telemetry.

stories.title: Using Cyber Decoys to Strengthen Detection and Response
stories.abstract: CISA has published new guidance on deploying cyber decoys to identify and hinder attackers operating within internal networks. These deceptive assets are designed to expose adversaries who leverage legitimate credentials or living-off-the-land techniques to move laterally and conduct unauthorized discovery.
stories.why: Decoys provide high-fidelity alerts for detecting sophisticated intruders who have already bypassed perimeter defenses and are operating within a compromised environment.

stories.title: Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists
stories.abstract: Iranian state-sponsored actors are deploying a Windows-based backdoor dubbed CHOSEN BRICK to conduct surveillance on dissidents, journalists, and activists. The malware leverages Telegram for command-and-control, enabling attackers to exfiltrate communications, capture screenshots, and record audio via compromised devices.
stories.why: This highlights the continued use of legitimate messaging platforms for covert C2 infrastructure and targeted espionage against high-risk individuals.

stories.title: Spain gets its first taste of AI-aided cyber attack
stories.abstract: The Spanish Data Protection Agency reported the country's first confirmed data breach executed by an AI agent. The automated system leveraged a large language model to conduct a multi-stage exfiltration attack, prompting regulators to demand an urgent reevaluation of current data security frameworks.
stories.why: This incident marks a shift toward automated, AI-driven exploitation, signaling that traditional defensive perimeters may be insufficient against LLM-orchestrated attacks.

stories.title: Bransys ELD
stories.abstract: Bransys ELD devices contain multiple vulnerabilities, including hardcoded MQTT credentials and cleartext data transmission. Exploitation allows unauthorized access to sensitive telemetry data and firmware across various transportation carriers.
stories.why: Hardcoded credentials in critical transportation infrastructure allow attackers to intercept real-time fleet data and potentially compromise device firmware.
stories.action: Update Bransys ELD to version 11.00.00 or later for Android and 1.1.54 or later for iOS.

stories.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Flaw Exploited in the Wild, Enables Root Command Execution
stories.abstract: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of a critical vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway's AsyncOS software. The flaw, stemming from improper email parsing validation, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges on affected systems.
stories.why: This vulnerability grants full system control to remote attackers, posing a severe risk to perimeter security and internal network integrity.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for AsyncOS immediately.

stories.title: Maximum Severity GitLab Flaw Puts Supply Chains at Risk
stories.abstract: GitLab has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-85706, which carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0. CISA has confirmed that malicious actors are actively exploiting this flaw in both Community and Enterprise editions of the platform.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows unauthorized file access, potentially compromising entire software supply chains and sensitive source code repositories.
stories.action: Update all GitLab instances to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap
stories.abstract: Adversaries are increasingly leveraging AI to weaponize vulnerabilities and leaked credentials at speeds that outpace traditional security team response times. This acceleration creates a widening gap between initial exposure and successful exploitation, rendering standard manual triage processes insufficient for modern threat landscapes.
stories.why: Security teams must shift from reactive triage to automated, risk-based prioritization to counter AI-driven exploitation speed.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Electric GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings
stories.abstract: A critical authentication flaw in Mitsubishi Electric's GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings software allows local attackers to bypass password protections. By modifying memory during execution, unauthorized users can view, alter, or delete sensitive control programs within industrial environments.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables unauthorized manipulation of industrial control logic, posing a significant risk to operational integrity and safety in manufacturing environments.

stories.title: Hackers reveal how Flock cameras really track cars and people
stories.abstract: Security researchers successfully compromised a Flock Safety surveillance camera, gaining access to its internal software. The breach revealed the device's capability to capture millions of images and perform advanced analytics, including the identification of both pedestrians and vehicles.
stories.why: The incident exposes potential privacy risks and vulnerabilities in widespread automated license plate recognition systems used by law enforcement and private entities.

stories.title: Google says some Pixel phone owners were hacked in zero-day attacks
stories.abstract: Google has confirmed that a vulnerability within the modem firmware of certain Pixel devices is currently being subjected to limited, targeted exploitation by malicious actors.
stories.why: Exploitation of baseband firmware can allow remote code execution or unauthorized access, bypassing standard OS-level security protections.
stories.action: Check for and install the latest available Android security updates for your Pixel device.

stories.title: Critical Unbound DNSSEC Validator Flaw Could Allow RCE via a Malicious DNS Zone
stories.abstract: NLnet Labs released Unbound version 1.26.1 to address a critical heap overflow vulnerability within its DNSSEC validation logic. An attacker managing a malicious DNS zone could exploit this flaw to achieve remote code execution on systems running older versions of the resolver.
stories.why: Unbound is a widely deployed recursive DNS resolver; remote code execution vulnerabilities in core infrastructure components pose significant risks to network integrity.
stories.action: Update Unbound to version 1.26.1 immediately.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Electric CC-Link IE TSN Communication Protocol (Update A)
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in Mitsubishi Electric's CC-Link IE TSN protocol allows network-adjacent attackers to manipulate communication data. By injecting crafted packets at precise intervals, adversaries can disrupt control functions, leading to service outages or unintended operational behavior in affected MELSEC MX-R controllers.
stories.why: Exploitation of industrial control protocols can lead to physical process disruption and safety risks within critical infrastructure environments.

stories.title: Hitachi Energy FACTS Control Platform (FCP)
stories.abstract: Hitachi Energy identified vulnerabilities in its FACTS Control Platform (FCP) specifically affecting systems equipped with the GWS component deployed since 2020. Exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of critical power infrastructure components like SVC Light and Static Var Compensators.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact industrial control systems managing high-voltage power grids, posing significant risks to operational technology stability and infrastructure security.
stories.action: Review Hitachi Energy's advisory and apply recommended mitigations for GWS-equipped FACTS Control systems.

stories.title: Schneider Electric NetBotz 5 750/755
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has disclosed two critical vulnerabilities in NetBotz 5 750 and 755 environmental monitoring devices. These flaws, involving OS command injection and SQL injection, could allow unauthorized remote code execution and data access by attackers on the local network.
stories.why: Compromise of these monitors grants attackers visibility into physical security and environmental controls, potentially facilitating further lateral movement within the facility network.
stories.action: Update NetBotz 5 750 and 755 firmware to a version beyond 5.5.2.

stories.title: Schneider Electric PowerChute Serial Shutdown
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has identified an authentication vulnerability in PowerChute Serial Shutdown versions 1.6 and earlier. The flaw involves improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts, which could potentially allow unauthorized access or operational disruption within managed UPS environments.
stories.why: Exploitation could lead to unauthorized system access or service outages in critical infrastructure environments relying on these power management tools.
stories.action: Update PowerChute Serial Shutdown to the latest version provided by Schneider Electric.

stories.title: Microsoft Issues Emergency Fixes After Massive Patch Tuesday
stories.abstract: Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to address technical regressions introduced during the recent Patch Tuesday cycle. These fixes resolve stability and functional problems caused by the initial batch of security patches deployed earlier this month.
stories.why: Unexpected post-patch instability can disrupt critical infrastructure and force emergency maintenance windows, potentially leaving systems vulnerable during the remediation process.
stories.action: Check for and install the latest out-of-band updates from Microsoft.

stories.title: Schneider Electric Modicon M340 Controller and Communication Modules
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has identified a security vulnerability affecting several Modicon M340 programmable automation controllers and associated Ethernet communication modules. The company is currently evaluating the impact and potential remediation steps for these industrial control system components.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial controllers can allow unauthorized access or disruption of critical operational technology environments.
stories.action: Monitor the Schneider Electric security portal for upcoming firmware updates and mitigation guidance.

stories.title: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens
stories.abstract: A Brazilian banking malware campaign, tracked as REF9334, is deploying a toolkit dubbed KREMLIN. This malware circumvents browser security controls to force-install malicious extensions on Chrome and Edge, enabling the theft of session tokens, credentials, and other sensitive user data.
stories.why: The ability to bypass browser-level extension installation protections poses a significant risk to session integrity and credential security for enterprise users.

stories.title: LausivLoader analysis, or how to pass data between malware stages, (Thu, Sep 17th)
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a new malware strain dubbed LausivLoader, distributed via phishing emails masquerading as business inquiries. The loader employs sophisticated techniques to pass data between execution stages, complicating detection and analysis for defenders monitoring email gateways.
stories.why: Understanding novel multi-stage loading mechanisms is critical for improving endpoint detection and response strategies against evolving obfuscation tactics.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-926)
stories.abstract: Google has released a security update for Chrome to address multiple vulnerabilities. Users running versions earlier than 153.0.8010.48 are susceptible to potential exploitation and should transition to the latest stable release immediately.
stories.why: Unpatched browser vulnerabilities are primary vectors for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 153.0.8010.48 or later.

stories.title: Adversary simulation: what you need to know
Zero-Day Flaw in TP-Link Cameras Enables Eavesdropping
Ransomware incidents in Japan in the first half of 2026: Investigation of The Gentlemen’s infrastructure and evidence of Qilin's AI use
stories.abstract: Ransomware attacks in Japan increased by nearly 5% during the first half of 2026. The Gentlemen emerged as the primary threat actor, while Qilin demonstrated the integration of artificial intelligence into its operations. Small and medium-sized enterprises remain the most frequent targets.
stories.why: The shift toward AI-assisted ransomware and the targeting of smaller, less-resourced organizations highlights evolving adversary tactics and broader attack surface risks.

stories.title: U.S. Seizes NightmareStresser Domains Linked to Hundreds of Thousands of DDoS Attacks
stories.abstract: Federal authorities have dismantled NightmareStresser, a long-standing DDoS-for-hire service, by seizing its primary web domains. The operation effectively terminates the platform's ability to facilitate distributed denial-of-service attacks for paying customers.
stories.why: This disruption removes a significant, accessible tool used by threat actors to launch disruptive attacks against online infrastructure.

stories.title: Revolut Data Breach: 5 Months, 680 High-Profile Accounts, $3M Ransom
stories.abstract: Financial services firm Revolut reportedly suffered a five-month security compromise after attackers successfully impersonated an Italian government entity. The breach exposed sensitive data belonging to 680 high-profile accounts, resulting in a $3 million ransom demand.
stories.why: This incident highlights the effectiveness of sophisticated social engineering and impersonation tactics against internal corporate verification processes.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells
stories.abstract: Unauthenticated attackers are exploiting a critical vulnerability in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin for WordPress. The flaw allows remote actors to upload arbitrary files, enabling the deployment of PHP webshells and full remote code execution on affected sites.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in widely used e-commerce plugins provide attackers with a direct path to server compromise and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin to the latest available version immediately.

stories.title: Ransomware Attacks on Manufacturers Surge as Supply Chain Risk Grows
stories.abstract: Ransomware activity targeting the manufacturing sector increased by 40% during the first quarter of 2026. Threat actors are specifically leveraging operational downtime and supply chain vulnerabilities to maximize the impact of their extortion efforts.
stories.why: Manufacturing environments face heightened risks of prolonged operational disruption and cascading supply chain failures when targeted by ransomware.

stories.title: Cyber Adversary Simulation (CyAS): scheme documents now available
CISA decides weekly vulnerability bulletin isn't necessary anymore
Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution
stories.abstract: The Issabel PBX framework is currently under active exploitation due to a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-89026. This flaw stems from a hard-coded credential issue, allowing remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary operating system commands on affected systems.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in unified communications infrastructure provide attackers with a direct foothold into internal networks and sensitive voice traffic.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for the Issabel Framework immediately.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE
stories.abstract: A Chinese-linked threat actor, identified as UTA0560, targeted NGOs using a spear-phishing campaign. The attackers leveraged a zero-day exploit chain involving Google Chrome and Microsoft Windows vulnerabilities to install a JavaScript-based backdoor known as GRIMWEDGE.
stories.why: This demonstrates sophisticated exploitation of browser and OS primitives to achieve remote code execution against high-value targets.
stories.action: Ensure all Chrome and Windows instances are updated to the latest security versions.

stories.title: CISO's Expert Guide to Agentic Pentesting for Websites
stories.abstract: A new guide outlines how autonomous AI agents can be utilized for website penetration testing. It emphasizes the necessity of rigorous security requirements before deploying these automated tools against live production environments to address the widening gap between vulnerability disclosure and remediation.
stories.why: Automated agents can accelerate vulnerability discovery, but improper implementation risks unintended service disruption or unauthorized data exposure in production environments.

stories.title: ISC BIND security advisory (AV26-931)
stories.abstract: ISC has disclosed vulnerabilities affecting multiple versions of BIND 9, including the 9.18, 9.20, and 9.21 branches. Administrators should review the official BIND 9 vulnerability matrix to determine if their specific deployment requires an update to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: BIND is a critical component of internet infrastructure; unpatched vulnerabilities in DNS software can lead to service disruption or unauthorized system access.
stories.action: Review the ISC BIND vulnerability matrix and apply available patches for your specific version.

stories.title: Apple security advisory (AV26-930)
stories.abstract: Apple has released a comprehensive suite of security updates across its entire ecosystem, including iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, Safari, and Xcode. These patches address multiple vulnerabilities affecting various versions of the company's operating systems and software development tools.
stories.why: Unpatched Apple software remains a primary target for exploitation; maintaining current versions is essential to mitigate risks from known security flaws.
stories.action: Update all Apple devices and software to the latest available versions immediately.

stories.title: Oracle Corporation security advisory (AV26-929)
stories.abstract: Oracle has released its quarterly security updates addressing numerous vulnerabilities across a wide range of enterprise products, including the Helidon framework, Oracle Banking suites, and various Business Intelligence and Communications platforms.
stories.why: These patches address critical security flaws that could allow unauthorized access or system compromise in enterprise environments running Oracle software.
stories.action: Review the Oracle Critical Patch Update advisory and apply relevant patches to affected systems.

stories.title: N0va Phishkit Targets US and EU Businesses: A New Challenge for Identity Security
stories.abstract: A new phishing kit dubbed N0va is actively targeting North American and European enterprises. The campaign mimics legitimate services to hijack authentication processes, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts and cloud environments without deploying traditional malware.
stories.why: It highlights the increasing difficulty of detecting identity-based attacks that bypass perimeter defenses by abusing standard authentication workflows.

stories.title: Three Threat Groups Target Russian Enterprises With Backdoors, Ransomware, and Wipers
stories.abstract: Kaspersky researchers identified three distinct threat clusters—NightEagle, Hacking Cat, and Toy Ghouls—actively targeting Russian corporate networks. These groups utilize specialized backdoors, ransomware, and destructive wiper malware to compromise systems, with NightEagle specifically deploying novel methods for maintaining persistence and moving laterally.
stories.why: The emergence of multiple coordinated threat actors targeting regional infrastructure highlights evolving TTPs for persistence and destructive attacks in enterprise environments.

stories.title: HPE security advisory (AV26-928)
[Control Systems] Phoenix Contact security advisory (AV26-927)
stories.abstract: Phoenix Contact has identified multiple security vulnerabilities affecting several IO-Link master modules, including the ICE2 and ICE3 series. These flaws impact various hardware models running firmware versions prior to 1.7.4.
stories.why: Unpatched industrial control system components can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical operational technology environments.
stories.action: Update affected Phoenix Contact IO-Link master modules to firmware version 1.7.4 or later.

stories.title: Hackers claim breach of Russian election systems days before parliamentary vote
stories.abstract: An unidentified group of hackers asserts they successfully compromised digital infrastructure linked to Russia's upcoming parliamentary elections. The breach allegedly occurred shortly before the scheduled commencement of the voting process.
stories.why: State-level election infrastructure compromises represent significant geopolitical risks and potential precursors to disinformation campaigns or operational interference.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Thursday, September 17th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10098, (Thu, Sep 17th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center podcast for September 17, 2026, provides a daily summary of current cybersecurity events and emerging threats observed by the research community.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat intelligence helps security professionals identify patterns and adjust defensive postures against evolving attack vectors.

stories.title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
stories.abstract: WSO2 API Manager is currently under active attack due to a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-5430. The flaw stems from faulty cryptographic signature validation, allowing unauthorized actors to forge JSON Web Tokens and gain administrative access to affected systems.
stories.why: This bypass enables full account takeover, granting attackers complete control over API management infrastructure and sensitive downstream services.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from WSO2 immediately.

stories.title: mySCADA myPRO Manager
Siemens Reyrolle 7SR5
stories.abstract: Siemens has patched fourteen vulnerabilities affecting Reyrolle 7SR5 devices running firmware versions prior to 2.70. These flaws include critical issues such as out-of-bounds writes, authentication bypasses, and improper input validation that could potentially be exploited by attackers.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure hardware, with some flaws carrying high CVSS scores that could allow for unauthorized control or system compromise.
stories.action: Update Siemens Reyrolle 7SR5 firmware to version 2.70 or later.

stories.title: Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard
stories.abstract: Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard version 5.07.0923.01 contains critical vulnerabilities, including a hardcoded cryptographic key in the update controller. Exploitation allows attackers to push unauthorized updates, execute arbitrary code, or steal credentials to impersonate privileged users within maritime fleet management systems.
stories.why: These flaws enable full system compromise of critical transportation infrastructure, potentially allowing remote attackers to manipulate navigation or operational data.
stories.action: Contact Wärtsilä support to obtain and apply the necessary security patches for FOS-Onboard.

stories.title: Digital Watchdog VMAX DVR and NVR Product Lineups
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Digital Watchdog VMAX DVR and NVR product lines allow attackers to gain full administrative control. Exploitation enables unauthorized access to surveillance feeds, configuration changes, and the ability to use compromised hardware as a pivot point for network attacks.
stories.why: Compromised surveillance infrastructure provides attackers with persistent internal network access and sensitive physical security data.
stories.action: Check Digital Watchdog support for firmware updates and isolate affected devices from public networks.

stories.title: CareCam CM2507
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in CareCam CM2507 firmware version v251211.1507 expose devices to remote code execution, credential theft, and unauthorized control. These flaws include improper authentication, hardcoded credentials, and insecure storage of sensitive data, potentially allowing attackers to hijack live video feeds.
stories.why: Compromised IoT cameras in commercial facilities provide attackers with persistent surveillance access and a foothold for lateral movement within internal networks.
stories.action: Disable or isolate affected CareCam CM2507 units until a firmware patch is applied.

stories.title: Scans Targeting Hospitality Applications, (Wed, Sep 16th)
stories.abstract: Security researchers have identified unusual, anomalous traffic patterns targeting hospitality-related web applications. These requests appear to be part of a new scanning campaign, though the specific intent or underlying vulnerability being probed remains currently unidentified.
stories.why: Early detection of reconnaissance patterns allows security teams to proactively block malicious infrastructure before targeted exploitation attempts occur.

stories.title: Nonprofit that tracks meteors taken down by "critical blow" from a cyberattack
stories.abstract: The American Meteor Society, a nonprofit organization dedicated to tracking celestial events, has suspended operations following a severe cyberattack. The group expects to remain offline for several weeks while they work to recover their systems and restore data services.
stories.why: This incident highlights the vulnerability of niche research organizations to disruptive attacks that can halt long-term data collection and public scientific contributions.

stories.title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
stories.abstract: Security researchers observed a threat actor leveraging a remote code execution vulnerability in a Marimo notebook to compromise an SSH bastion. The entire transition from initial entry to reaching the target infrastructure occurred in just eight seconds.
stories.why: This demonstrates how rapidly attackers can pivot through cloud environments once they gain a foothold, highlighting the critical need for automated detection.

stories.title: New Chinese-Made ‘RatHat’ Android Malware Leverages AI to Steal Financial Data
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a novel Android malware strain named RatHat. This malicious software functions as a backdoor, granting attackers remote access to infected devices to exfiltrate sensitive financial information and perform unauthorized surveillance.
stories.why: It demonstrates evolving mobile threats that combine traditional backdoor functionality with advanced data theft techniques targeting financial applications.

stories.title: Can You Prove a New CVE Is Exploitable Before Attackers Do? Learn How in This Webinar
stories.abstract: Security teams struggle to determine if newly disclosed vulnerabilities are truly exploitable within their specific environments. As automated tools accelerate the timeline for weaponizing flaws, traditional, slow-moving risk assessment cycles leave organizations exposed to rapid exploitation.
stories.why: The widening gap between vulnerability disclosure and active exploitation renders static, periodic risk assessments insufficient for modern threat defense.

stories.title: Brevo supply-chain attack injected ClickFix scripts on customer sites
stories.abstract: Brevo suffered a supply-chain compromise after threat actors obtained a Cloudflare API key. The attackers leveraged this access to inject malicious ClickFix scripts into Brevo's infrastructure, which subsequently distributed malware to visitors of websites utilizing the company's embedded JavaScript services.
stories.why: Compromised third-party scripts represent a significant vector for watering hole attacks, potentially exposing end-users to credential theft or malware delivery.
stories.action: Audit third-party script integrations and review Cloudflare API key permissions.

stories.title: Siemens Teamcenter
stories.abstract: Siemens Teamcenter contains a reflected cross-site scripting flaw in its authentication redirect mechanism. Remote attackers can exploit this by sending malicious URLs to authenticated users, potentially allowing unauthorized data access or session manipulation.
stories.why: XSS in authentication flows can lead to session hijacking or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of legitimate users within sensitive engineering environments.
stories.action: Update Siemens Teamcenter to the latest versions specified in the vendor security advisory.
